session_label: Patna Madrasa Sulaimania MS no. 2 and backchain-mining pass
scope: Follow up the external new-leads review from a blank-slate posture. Mine the strongest candidate lead, Patna Madrasa Sulaimania / Sulaymaniyah MS no. 2, and retest adjacent edition, South Asian, MESTAP, Ilkhchi, and Turkish backchain routes. Register counts are not changed by this artifact.

method_summary.primary: Targeted web search in Persian, Latin transliteration, Turkish, and South Asian institutional terminology; direct page inspection for the surviving hits; comparison against the existing South Asia and edition-backchain search artifacts.
method_summary.source_weighting: Primary catalogue, repository, facsimile-series, and article pages were prioritized. Shop, Telegram, and aggregator pages are treated as acquisition or backchain leads unless they expose codex-level evidence.
method_summary.promotion_rule: A lead is not promoted to data/witness_register.json unless the evidence identifies Jahanshah/Cihansah Haqiqi rather than another Haqiqi, and gives enough manuscript-level detail to distinguish a codex, facsimile, or edition from a generic title hit.

external_review_follow_up.review_output: local artifact-review note; private reviewer path not deposited
accepted_points: Patna no. 2 needs an Indo-Persian Haqiqi homonym/disambiguation lane before any register promotion; Yusuf Hakiki is not the only relevant false-positive class for a South Asian Persian divan title.
The Blogfa For Tomorrow no. 126 listing is load-bearing and volatile; archive/stability handling should be explicit.
The listing's 126-page statement is a page-count, not necessarily a folio-count; it cannot be compared directly against witness folio counts without the facsimile or catalogue entry.
The Demirci 1997 page range needed direct PDF resolution because local artifacts mixed 127-134 and 127-138.
verified_after_review: Direct ISAM PDF inspection confirms the full article span as printed pages 127-138. Pages 137-138 are manuscript-image plates; pages 130-131 contain the core codicological descriptions for Suleymaniye Fatih 3808 and Ankara DTCF Ismail Saib I/2221.

The Blogfa listing was directly reachable on 2026-05-18 and contains the For Tomorrow no. 126 Divan-i Haqiqi entry, but Wayback availability/save attempts from this environment returned HTTP 429 or timed out.
held_points: Claude named possible Indo-Persian Haqiqi figures, but those names are treated only as search seeds here because they were not independently confirmed in this pass.

high_priority_findings.summary: A Majma-i Zakhair-i Islami facsimile-series list records a Divan-i Haqiqi, manuscript no. 2, Madrasa Sulaimania/Sulaymaniyah, Patna, India, as For Tomorrow no. 126, Persian poetry, 126 pages, color facsimile. A later Boroujerdi Library notice identifies a 2023 printed catalogue of the same Patna collection as containing bibliographic/codicological data and selected images for more than 200 manuscripts. Google Books and WorldCat now confirm the catalogue as a 364-page 2023 Majma-i Zakhair-i Islami publication by Tayebeh Hajj Baqerian, ISBN 9786223041525 / OCLC 1402253747, volume 128 of the Muarrifi-i Mirath-i makhtut series. This is the first concrete Patna Madrasa Sulaimania lead found in the project and is outside the previously probed Khuda Bakhsh/Bankipore Patna route.

why_not_register_yet: The accessible facsimile-list entry gives title, shelf/series number, institution, language, and page count, but not author heading, incipit, explicit, colophon, date, scribe, foliation, or first lines.
Haqiqi is a known homonym and can also function adjectivally; a title-only Divan-i Haqiqi in a South Asian Persian setting must be disambiguated before counting.
In a Patna / Indo-Persian library context, the homonym prior must include local or regional Persian-writing Haqiqi poets and Sufi figures, not only Yusuf Hakiki or Ottoman/Bektashi false positives.

The 126-page listing is not a folio count. Until the facsimile or catalogue entry is inspected, it should not be compared one-for-one against folio counts in BL Or 9493, Matenadaran 965, Fatih 3808, DTCF I/2221, or Tehran 8198.

The facsimile listing proves a concrete acquisition path. It does not by itself prove this is Jahanshah Qaraqoyunlu's Divan rather than another Haqiqi or an edition/facsimile title normalized by the publisher.
next_verification_steps: Use the new data/search_keys.json south_asian_haqiqi_homonym_treatment block as the intake checklist; extend it with named, source-confirmed Indo-Persian Haqiqi homonyms only after Storey, tazkira, or catalogue evidence is inspected.

Obtain the 2023 printed Patna Madrasa Sulaimania catalogue and inspect entry no. 2. Prioritize this over generic catalogue searching because the launch notice says it contains codicological descriptions and selected images.
Obtain or view For Tomorrow no. 126 from Majma-i Zakhair-i Islami; record title page, author heading, incipit, explicit, foliation/page count, date, scribe, and any colophon.
Compare at least three first lines against known Jahanshah witnesses: BL Or 9493, Matenadaran 965, Suleymaniye Fatih 3808, Ankara DTCF I/2221, and Tehran University 8198.
If the evidence confirms Jahanshah/Cihansah, add a candidate entry to the register using an existing allowed verification_status unless the schema is explicitly extended.

high_priority_findings.summary: The previously unretrieved Demirci 1997 article is now hosted by ISAM with a downloadable PDF. Direct inspection resolves the full article span as printed pages 127-138; pages 137-138 are manuscript-image plates. The article directly describes the two Turkish witnesses: Suleymaniye Fatih 3808 and Ankara DTCF Ismail Saib I/2221.

source_evidence.observed: The record identifies Jale Demirci, 1997, Turkoloji Dergisi XII/1, pp. 127-138, with a 1.33 MB PDF.

The article states that, beyond the British Museum witness, two previously unmentioned copies exist: one in Suleymaniye Library and one in Ankara University DTCF Library. It gives dimensions, folios, line counts, contents, and copy notes for both. The PDF has 13 pages: a cover page plus printed article pages 127-138. Printed pages 137-138 are manuscript-image plates, so the ISAM 127-138 range is the complete article/plate span; older 127-134 citations should be treated as legacy or shortened citations unless the citing source is being quoted verbatim.

codex_data_recovered.suleymaniye_fatih_3808: Fatih 3808, copied by Mustafa Bey Osman Pasha; 24.4 x 15.6 cm; 107 folios; 10-12 lines/page; ff. 1a-71b Persian poems and ff. 72a-107a Turkish poems; 96 Turkish ghazals and 29 rubais; nasta'liq; described as carefully copied and well preserved. The article gives opening and closing lines but no paper, binding, illumination, or decoration data.
codex_data_recovered.ankara_dtcf_ismail_saib_1_2221: Ankara University DTCF Library, Ismail Saib I.2221; 26 folios; 13 x 18 cm with 11.5 x 16.5 cm writing area; nasta'liq; copied by al-Hac Huseyin, completed 12 Muharram 1290 AH; contains 80 Turkish ghazals, lacks the Persian section and rubais found in the other two witnesses; no paper, binding, illumination, or decoration data.

implications: The register and README should no longer say Demirci 1997 was not retrieved in open access.
Use 127-138 for the complete Demirci 1997 article citation in non-verbatim metadata. Preserve 127-134 only where it is quoted from Macit 2000 or another source as a historical citation.
Demirci strongly supports Ankara DTCF as the institution for Ismail Saib I/2221, while the Islamisation DB/Ataturk University conflict remains worth institutional follow-up.
The article improves codicological description but does not solve the main decoration/material-data gap.
